none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

results.references: - Guanghui Lan and Yu Yang. [Accelerated Stochastic Algorithms for Nonconvex Finite-sum and Multi-block Optimization](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.05411v5). 2019 (preprint 2018; version 5 consulted). Complexity: $O\!\left(1+\sqrt{L/\mu}\,(1+\mu\Delta/\varepsilon^2)\log(2+L/\mu)\right)$ fixed-budget exact-gradient calls, including initialization, for single-component unconstrained RapGrad to obtain $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$. Here $\mu=\min\{L,\max\{\rho,\varepsilon^2/\Delta\}\}$ is a positive weak-convexity upper bound when $\Delta>0$; $\Delta=0$ requires only returning $x_0$.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained, globally L-smooth, rho-weakly convex objectives on a real Hilbert space: f(x)+(rho/2)||x||² is convex. Nonconvex objectives are permitted; rho=0 gives the convex subcase. L>0 and rho>=0.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Every reply is the exact gradient at the queried point, for every history and oracle seed. No function values or noisy gradients are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothWeaklyConvex.lean: spec.admissible, HasGradientAt requirement; spec.Query and spec.Reply.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space. Public information includes L, rho, Delta, epsilon and x0, with Delta>=0 and epsilon>0. A global lower bound exists with f(x0)-lower<=Delta; neither the lower bound nor f is public. Allowed algorithms use positive, predetermined scalar gradient steps and retain the queried iterate with smallest observed gradient norm.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothWeaklyConvex.lean: Params; spec.Public; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible; gdFamily; spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The output must satisfy E[||gradient f(output)||²]<=epsilon². It must be measurable, and its squared gradient norm must be integrable. gdFamily requires outputting the retained best queried iterate.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee is an expectation over the product of algorithm-seed and oracle-seed laws, under a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth weakly convex stationarity with exact gradients and an initial objective-gap bound is an established optimization formulation. The setup additionally restricts admissible algorithms to predetermined positive-step gradient descent.
